title: Energy, digital, and defence transitions are intensifying mineral demand while refining and trade controls concentrate supply-chain risk
source_unit: International Energy Agency, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026
geography: Global critical-mineral markets, refining and investment, energy and technology value chains, and Latin America and the Caribbean

denominator.unit: global critical-mineral market and energy-technology demand frame

battery_demand.unit: terawatt-hours of global battery demand in 2025, more than

battery_demand_change.unit: percent growth in global battery demand in 2025, more than

energy_sector_share_demand_growth.unit: percent of growth in demand for key energy minerals driven by the energy sector in 2025, approximately

mineral_demand_growth_rate.unit: percent average annual growth in demand for key energy minerals in recent years, approximately

observations.method: IEA synthesis of market data, technology deployment, company reporting, and scenario-based mineral demand analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Demand and deployment measures do not establish completed projects, local extraction or refining benefits, environmental burden, affordability, or durable consumer access to downstream technologies.
observations.subgroup: Energy-technology producers, mineral firms, refiners, infrastructure providers, governments, workers, communities, and downstream users of batteries, grids, digital systems, and defence technologies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rapid demand growth can support investment, recycling, technological substitution, and wider access if supply-chain expansion is governed, diversified, and linked to local capability and benefit sharing.

top_refined_supplier_share_2025.unit: percent average share of the top refined supplier across energy minerals in 2025

top_refined_supplier_share_2020.unit: percent average share of the top refined supplier across energy minerals in 2020

dominant_supply_growth_share.unit: percent of total refined-supply growth from 2023 to 2025 accounted for by Indonesia and China across key markets, more than

refining_diversification_exception.value: rare earth refining concentration declined modestly with new US projects and increased Malaysian production

observations.method: IEA comparison of country-level mining and refining production, supply growth, and concentration across key energy minerals.
observations.uncertainty: Refining concentration is not identical to mine ownership, finished-product dependence, substitution time, inventory, or political leverage; the exception does not remove broader concentration.
observations.subgroup: Dominant and non-dominant refining countries, mining and processing firms, downstream manufacturers, importing states, workers, and communities near extraction and processing.
observations.counterinterpretation: Targeted investment and policy support can create diversification, and concentrated suppliers may still provide reliable or lower-cost inputs under stable trade conditions.

observations.period: 2025-2026; export controls, prices, and downstream exposure

denominator.unit: critical-mineral trade-control and downstream production-risk frame

strategic_minor_mineral_price_change.unit: fold increase in strategic minor mineral prices through 2025 and early 2026, more than

chinese_controlled_mineral_codes_change.unit: fold increase in mineral tariff codes subject to Chinese export controls since 2023

rare_earth_downstream_risk.unit: US dollars per year of downstream production outside China potentially at risk under full implementation of expanded rare-earth controls, estimated

graphite_downstream_risk.unit: US dollars per year of downstream production outside China potentially at risk under full battery-grade graphite disruption, estimated

observations.method: IEA analysis of export-control announcements, mineral prices, supply-chain structure, and modeled downstream production exposure.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates are scenario-based exposure calculations, not realized losses, outages, consumer-price effects, or proof that controls will be fully implemented or sustained.
observations.subgroup: Mineral exporters and importers, automakers, battery and semiconductor firms, energy and defence industries, workers, governments, and downstream consumers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Controls can motivate substitution, stockpiling, recycling, new entrants, and negotiated supply arrangements; risk may be buffered by inventories or alternative technologies.

observations.period: 2025-2035; Latin American value-chain opportunity and capacity constraints

denominator.unit: Latin American and Caribbean critical-mineral production and refining frame

regional_copper_mine_share.unit: percent of global copper mine output produced by Latin America and the Caribbean, approximately

regional_lithium_supply_share.unit: percent of global lithium supply produced by Latin America and the Caribbean, approximately

regional_refining_share.unit: share of mined output of key energy minerals refined within the region, approximately

potential_regional_value.unit: US dollars of potential annual economic value by 2035 under expanded regional processing, approximately

capacity_constraints.value: financing costs, power and water infrastructure, technology, skills, and local-stakeholder engagement

observations.method: IEA regional analysis of mineral production, refining, value-chain scenarios, and enabling conditions in Latin America and the Caribbean.
observations.uncertainty: The potential value is a modeled opportunity, not committed investment, completed refining, public revenue, local employment, environmental approval, or community benefit.
observations.subgroup: Latin American and Caribbean governments, mining and processing firms, local communities, workers, infrastructure providers, financiers, and global downstream buyers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Local processing can raise value capture and bargaining capacity, but extraction-led growth can also intensify water, land, environmental, fiscal, and distributional conflicts without safeguards.

related_sources.claim: IEA medium- and long-term demand projections for 37 critical minerals across scenarios and technology cases.
Official IEA report landing page, publication date, scope, data explorer, and policy/workforce framing.

boundary: This record adds a mineral-demand-to-refining-concentration-to-export-control-to-downstream-production and regional-value-capture route. It is not mine-level incidence, respondent data, proof of completed projects, realized shortages, consumer-price effects, local consent, or evidence that mineral dependence automatically creates geopolitical leverage.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 landing page, market overview, executive summary, and outlook pages were reviewed; demand, refining concentration, export-control, modeled downstream exposure, investment, recycling, Latin American production, refining, value, and capacity-constraint claims were cross-checked.
